ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under PCMLTFA and SOR/2002-184: identity verification of all directors, officers, authorized signatories, and every individual with significant control; enhanced due diligence triggers for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) under ss. 11.13-11.16 of SOR/2002-184; automated screening against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, UK Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada Canadian sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act), and the FINTRAC administrative penalty list; red-flag analysis for nominee directors, opaque corporate chains, and shell-company indicators; corroboration of source of funds for intended AdMob/AppLovin payout flows; continuous re-screening obligation for the life of the corporate relationship and before any disbursement transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (OneStop Business Registry), operated by the BC Registrar of Companies, available at https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca; federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (NUANS Name Search and New Registration System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A British Columbia company name must be composed of a distinctive element, a descriptive element (optional), and a statutory legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or 'Societe a responsabilite limitee' for bilingual use); names must be freely usable in Latin script, using English or French characters; non-Latin-script brand names must be transliterated into Latin script and the Latin transliteration constitutes the registerable name; the name must not be confusingly similar to any existing BC corporate, extraprovincial, or numbered company record and must not falsely suggest an entity of a different type or jurisdiction.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Co-operative (requires prior consent of the registrar)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, setting out grounds distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting record and proposing not more than three alternative names; reconsideration is processed through Corporate Online and carries a statutory fee; if the reconsideration fails, the applicant may file a fresh name reservation (the 56-day reservation window cannot be extended); administrative exhaustion is required before judicial review to the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 413, within 60 days of the final administrative decision. For a federal CBCA name, a similar Name Reconsideration filing is made to Corporations Canada within 30 days and the NUANS name reservation window is 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry (unregulated ISIC 5820 software publisher) provided that the registered office and registered records office in British Columbia are located at a physical street address within the province; a post office box is prohibited; the virtual office may be operated by a lawyer, notary, or corporate service provider accepting service of process and mail forwarding; the company must maintain demonstrable commercial substance in the form of its own bank account, books and records, and contracts with AdMob/AppLovin counterparties in its own legal name.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 3-5% annual probability). The BC Registrar of Companies relies predominantly on documentary filings and does not conduct routine unannounced physical inspections of registered offices for low-risk non-regulated publishers; unannounced on-site verification arises only when inconsistent UBO/transparency filings, an active Canada Revenue Agency audit, or third-party complaints create reasonable suspicion. A hyper-casual gaming company without a regulated payment-services licence presents no heightened inspection trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57; core provisions: s. 10 (incorporation method), s. 27 (articles), s. 30 (registration), s. 111 (registered office), s. 121 (first directors); supplementary rules under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44 where federal applicability arises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Registry Division), Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles and Articles of Incorporation (Corporate Online e-Filing Form)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the BC Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued without an escrow deposit or capital contribution, and subscribers may be credited as fully paid in accordance with the articles.

stage_2.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscribers present adopt the Articles of Incorporation and hereby ratify their respective share subscriptions, with the consideration credited as fully paid per the authorized capital rules; (2) the registered office be and is hereby established at the Company’s principal physical premises in British Columbia and the registered office representative is appointed; (3) the initial directors named in the Notice of Articles shall serve until the first annual general meeting; (4) the directors are authorized to appoint officers, adopt by-laws, issue share certificates, open banking accounts supporting AdMob and AppLovin payout rails, and execute all filings, registrations, and licences incidental to the corporate formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search (NUANS) via Corporate Online or an accredited service provider. Reserve the corporate name for 56 days by filing an electronic Name Reservation Request. Ensure the proposed name does not conflict with existing BC or federal trademarks and contains a legal element such as 'Ltd.' or 'Corp.'
required_dossiers: Consent to name usage from any named individual
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusing similarity, submit a revised name with a new NUANS report; expedited re-review via Corporate Online help desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Articles and Articles of Incorporation electronically, listing the incorporators, first directors, share structure, and registered office address. Pay the statutory filing fee by corporate credit card or BC OnLine account. Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the company obtains legal existence.
required_dossiers: Incorporators' consents to act as directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries a deficiency, amend and resubmit the Article reinstatement within 14 days; retroactive correction applies upon acceptance and Certificate reissuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Initial Corporate Records and Board Organization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural board meeting (physical at the registered office or by unanimous written resolution if permitted by the articles). Adopt the corporate by-laws, approve the share subscription, elect officers, approve the share register and corporate minute book, and confirm the registered office designation.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the inaugural board meeting
Notice of first directors and registered office record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure defective minutes by filing supplemental written resolutions and ratifying actions retroactively under s. 121 of the BC Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number Registration and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Ministry of Finance (Provincial Sales Tax Branch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number (BN) via Business Registration Online or paper RC1 form. Register for GST/HST account (non-resident or resident status), payroll deductions account (CRA) if employees are hired, and BC Provincial Sales Tax account. The BN becomes the universal identifier for tax filings with CRA and provincial authorities.
required_dossiers: Notice of Directors and Registered Office
Parent entity tax identification if foreign-controlled
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is queried, provide an amended RC1 with corrected fiscal details; CRA reassigns accounts within 3 business days after re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Digital Payout Rails Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or authorized credit union; AdMob and AppLovin payout partner onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate demand deposit account at a Canadian banking institution. Present incorporation certificate, BN confirmation, directors' resolution authorizing the account, and KYC documentation for beneficial owners. Submit the account details and tax withholding forms (W-8BEN-E for the company) to AdMob and AppLovin to configure payment rails.
required_dossiers: W-8BEN-E form for cross-border payment platforms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, supply additional KYC and a confirmatory search report (BC Registry) proving no corporate veil issues; appeal the decision as an interbranch escalation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver Licence Department or applicable municipal authority; local fire and building inspection office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal Business Licence for the registered office (home-based or standalone office). Submit lease ownership attestation, floor area plan, and a declaration of business activity. Where an office lease is entered, obtain an occupancy permit and pass a basic fire safety inspection prior to employee workspace activation.
required_dossiers: WorksafeBC employer registration (if employees are engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is refused for zoning non-compliance, apply for a Variance Permit or relocate the registered office to a permitted commercial zone; fire safety deficiencies are cured by installation of required extinguishers and exit signage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable (ISIC 5820 software publishing is not a listed industrial activity under the British Columbia Industrial Licensing Regulation, BC Reg. 39/2014).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no provincial manufacturing or operational licence is mandated for hyper-casual mobile game publishing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Category 2 – no physical facility, no atmospheric emissions, no wastewater generation, and no hazardous waste handling attributable to a software-only publisher)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No statutory threshold applies to virtual digital publishing; in the event of future office expansion, Volatile Organic Compound (VOC) and wastewater limits under the Environmental Management Act, SBC 2003, c. 53 and its Permitting Regulation would apply solely to leased premises mechanical systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required under the BC Fire Code for any leased office space, including inspection of emergency exits and suppression equipment; structural load clearance is obtained from the building's municipal occupancy permit; WorksafeBC occupational clearance is triggered if employees are present, requiring OHS compliance, employer registration, and a health and safety program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO), CRA My Business Account portal, GST/HST NETFILE, T2 NETFILE. Provincial component: British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch (administering the 7% Provincial Sales Tax), and the BC Corporate Registry for provincial incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a BC-incorporated Business Corporation: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia); (2) Apply for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO), by telephone, or by mailing/faxing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number); the corporate income tax program account is BN-RC and the GST/HST program account is BN-RT (yielding the 15-character GST/HST registration number); register payroll via BN-RP if employees are engaged; (3) a non-resident publisher of digital games must use the simplified non-resident GST/HST registration (Form GST494) and is required to register regardless of the C$30,000 small-supplier threshold, and the CRA may require appointment of a Canadian tax representative; (4) a foreign-owned resident BC corporation obtains the BN through the same CRA process and must file the annual T2 corporate income tax return and periodic GST/HST returns electronically once prescribed thresholds are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act (ITA): Canadian-resident corporations are taxable on worldwide income; there is no US-style check-the-box or flow-through classification. Applicable rates: federal 15% general / 9% small business (CCPC) plus BC provincial 12% general / 2% small business (combined 27% general / 11% small business where the corporation qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation); a non-resident-controlled Canadian corporation remains resident and fully taxable in Canada, with no territorial exemption for foreign business income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada. Relevant statutory elections and mechanical regimes: (i) ITA s. 85 rollover election for tax-deferred transfers of property into the corporation; (ii) GST/HST closely related corporation election under ETA s. 156 (Form RC2501) to simplify inter-corporate supplies; (iii) voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s. 240(3) to claim input tax credits (ITCs) where the small-supplier threshold is not exceeded; (iv) hybrid mismatch rules under ITA s. 18.4–18.6 (effective for payments made after 30 June 2022) operate mechanically to deny deductions or include amounts where cross-border arrangements create deduction/non-inclusion or double-non-taxation outcomes — no election disapplies these rules; (v) functional currency election for computing Canadian tax in USD (ITA s. 261) where the corporation keeps books in a prescribed foreign currency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — value-added Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST). British Columbia applies only the 5% federal GST; BC does not participate in the HST and separately imposes the 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST) under the BC Provincial Sales Tax Act (PST applies to prewritten software sold in tangible media but not to digitally downloaded software and is administered by the BC Consumer Taxation Branch).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (GST/HST small-supplier threshold) measured as cumulative consideration for taxable supplies, including zero-rated exports, made in Canada within a single calendar quarter or the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. No threshold applies to non-resident suppliers making specified supplies (digitally delivered software, games, and intangible personal property) to Canadian recipients, who must register for GST/HST regardless of revenue level. The resident CA_CORP should consider voluntary registration even below C$30,000 to recover input tax credits on development, cloud infrastructure, and advertising inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or e-invoice pre-authorization regime. The CRA operates a voluntary pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework aligned with the Peppol network. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding C$1M (GST/HST NETFILE or approved EDI software), and the CRA assigns annual, quarterly, or monthly reporting frequencies based on the registrant's taxable supply volume. Every invoice or receipt must contain the ETA s. 221 prescribed particulars, including the supplier's 15-character BN-RT registration number, the amount of tax charged, total consideration, and, for zero-rated exports, a clear zero-rating indication. Books and records must be retained for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under s. 21.1 of Part V, Schedule VI, Excise Tax Act, supplies of intangible personal property (IPP) — including hyper-casual games, downloadable software, in-app content, and licences/ad-serving rights — are zero-rated when made to a recipient who is a non-resident of Canada and not registered for GST/HST, unless the IPP is supplied for use in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada (consumer-use exclusion). Ad-supported export revenue (AdMob/AppLovin payouts) qualifies where the monetized end users are non-Canadian and payment originates from the non-resident ad network; substantiation requires two non-conflicting indicators of recipient location such as billing address, IP geolocation, app-store territory, or device storefront country code. Supplies to Canadian end users attract 5% GST. B2B digital services procured from non-registered non-residents (e.g., ad-tech platforms) are subject to the reverse charge under ETA s. 218.01, requiring the Canadian recipient to self-assess 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — not required for intangible digital exports; the B13A / Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) applies to physical goods with a value exceeding C$2,000, and would be required only if the exporter ships physical media (e.g., USB/SD cards) outside Canada.

Bill of Lading / digital delivery evidence — for digital downloads, substitute app-store territory reports, AdMob/AppLovin payout statements, download logs, and server-side delivery records evidencing supply to non-resident end users in lieu of transport documents.

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank-issued inward remittance advices, SWIFT MT103 records, or EPRS statements proving settlement of export invoiced amounts from non-resident payors; retain together with the executed licence agreement, zero-rated invoices, and CRA registration confirmation (BN-RT) for a minimum of six years for s. 21.1 audit support.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within the normal 4-year limitation period for GST/HST (ETA s. 298), and without time limit where the registrant has made a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, fraud, or wilful default. A failed zero-rating claim results in reversal to 5% GST, disallowance or debit of ITCs, interest at the prescribed daily compounded rate, and penalties: ETA s. 285(1) — the greater of C$250 and 25% of the false tax amount for false statements; ETA s. 285(2) — 50% of the false tax amount for knowingly false statements; ETA s. 280.1 failure-to-file penalties; and director's liability under ETA s. 323 for unremitted GST/HST. Proven evasion (ETA s. 327 / s. 237(1)) carries fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years. The 180-day parameter is the commercial and Export Development Canada (EDC) benchmark for export collection and a CRA administrative-reasonableness reference; no separate statutory FX repatriation deadline exists under the ETA, but unrepatriated or related-party export receivables may attract ITA transfer-pricing or attribution scrutiny on audit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in conjunction with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); Canada does not operate exchange controls and the Bank of Canada does not administer or approve ordinary foreign exchange transactions, which fall under commercial bank dealing and FINTRAC supervision for reporting purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions; Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction. Dividend and profit remittance to non-residents is unrestricted, subject to Canadian solvency and corporate law tests, and triggers Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, generally reduced to 15% or lower under reciprocity treaties such as the Canada-US and Canada-UK treaties). No central bank authorization is required for periodic profit distribution or capital repatriation, but banks will require documentary support and FATCA/CRS declarations for the remitting entity and ultimate beneficial owners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds, including digital advertising and ad-network settlement receipts. An entity resident in British Columbia may lawfully maintain multi-currency USD operating accounts, convert to CAD at commercial rates, and use proceeds for current expenses without finance ministry approval. Export receipts are nonetheless included in taxable income and must be reported in Canadian dollars for income tax purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Operating Account / CAD-USD Dual-Currency Clearing Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Sub-Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with legal constraints. Canada does not issue EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) licenses; non-bank payment service providers, including foreign EMIs operating into Canada, must register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act if they provide payment or FX services to Canadian residents. A BC-incorporated company can contract with regulated PSPs such as Payoneer, Airwallex, or Wise to receive USD ad-network settlement, but the cleaner and more durable route is a domestic bank account at a Schedule I bank, with the PSP used exclusively as a treasury accelerator and not as primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or remote-video identity verification is mandatory under PCMLTFA customer due diligence rules. Schedule I Canadian banks generally require at least one director or authorized signatory to appear in person at a Canadian branch or before a Canadian notary/commissioner of oaths for corporate account opening. Fully remote onboarding is available only where the bank already holds an existing relationship or where an approved digital identity verification provider is deployed; otherwise corporate KYC will require notarized board resolutions, certified passports, beneficial ownership disclosure, and independent source-of-funds evidence for all directors and 25% or greater beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-ticket inbound settlement from foreign ad networks (AdMob, AppLovin) flagged as possible structuring or unexplained digital receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide signed platform publisher agreements, SDK payment dashboards, payout reconciliations, historical transaction logs, and a board-approved written AML compliance program with designated AML officer, transaction monitoring thresholds, and ongoing source-of-funds documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors/beneficial owners or an interposed offshore parent entity causing opaque ownership structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver corporate organizational chart, shareholders register, beneficial ownership declaration, certificate of good standing, notarized passports, residential address proof for principals, and source-of-wealth evidence for each 25% or greater shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No Canadian physical premises, employees, or demonstrable economic substance in BC despite a BC incorporation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce BC registered office documentation, registrar attestation, management contracts, publishing/licensing agreements, IP assignment records, and a written explanation of the digitally-native hyper-casual publishing model with geographic nexus through contract counterparties and treasury management in Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual USD/EUR wires from high-risk jurisdictions or inconsistent SWIFT purpose codes on outbound royalty/contractor payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain an intercompany cash-flow map, commercial invoices, royalty/licensing agreements, and a treasury policy restricting all cross-border flows to designated SWIFT-participating clearing banks with aligned ISO 20022 purpose codes, OFAC/PEP screening, and independent audit trail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity injections or shareholder loans, the non-resident lender or shareholder should transmit a SWIFT MT103 wire to the entity's CAD-denominated operating or capital escrow account using ISO 20022 purpose code categories for equity (e.g., 'EQUI' or bank-mapped capital transfer code) and clear narrative 'Capital Injection / Shareholder Loan'. The receiving bank will require a board resolution approving the injection, a subscription/shareholder agreement, FATCA/CRS Form W-8BEN-E, source-of-funds evidence, and foreign exchange reporting if the wire exceeds FINTRAC thresholds. CAD settlement typically occurs via Lynx high-value payment system on a same-day or next-day basis.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for non-documentary cross-border payments such as royalties, affiliated service fees, advertising traffic acquisition, and contractor settlements, embedding ISO 20022 remittance information referencing underlying invoices. For documented trade, equipment, or large licensing milestones, use commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT710 and settled through the confirming bank's correspondent network. USD clearing is executed through Canadian bank NY branches over Fedwire/CHIPS, while CAD legs clear via Lynx; all outbound payments must be OFAC-screened and aligned with the entity's AML/ATF program.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (outright CAD/USD contracts) with board-approved treasury policy
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-convertible or illiquid currencies used for ad-revenue exposures outside G10 economies, subject to bank credit documentation
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD principal and interest exchanges) for monetization of term ad-network receivables or intercompany loans

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; daily interest on unpaid amounts; gross negligence penalty up to 50%; possible director liability for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Varies by reporting period; annual filers must file no later than three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts penalties under the Excise Tax Act plus daily interest on unremitted amounts; CRA may issue demands, impose repeat-penalty amounts, and hold directors liable for unremitted net tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic revenue or asset threshold applies to ordinary private companies under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act. A statutory audit is mandatory for reporting issuers, and for private companies when voting shareholders have not unanimously waived the requirement or members holding 10% of voting shares require an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-reporting private corporations may use Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); reporting issuers and certain widely held corporations must use IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, the transparency register of individuals with significant control must be maintained at the company's records address. Any share transfer that creates or changes significant control must be recorded within 15 days of becoming aware of the change. No separate UBO schedule is filed with the BC Registrar; however, the annual report filing confirms the company is maintaining its required statutory records.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 20,000 for a full audit engagement when required; no audit cost applies if unanimous shareholder waiver is in place
